title: Quasi-finiteness descends for a finitely presented affine model
statement: Let $(I,\leq)$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, let $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ be a directed system of commutative rings, and let $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ be its colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a finitely presented $A_{i_0}$-algebra $B_0$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $B_i=A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$ for $i\geq i_0$ and $B=A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$; these tensor products of commutative algebras are the pushouts whose spectra are the affine fibre products [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. If $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], then for some $i\geq i_0$ the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is quasi-finite.
